sections.title: Introduction
sections.text:
Welcome back. Today's story is one of the best-known stories in the whole Bible: Noah and the ark. Many of us first heard it as children, with pictures of animals lined up two by two and a bright rainbow at the end. But this story is far more than a children's tale. It is a story about sin and judgment, about one man's faithful obedience, and about the God who keeps His promises.

The story is found in Genesis chapters six through nine. As we listen, think about this question: what does it look like to obey God when no one else around you is doing it?

sections.title: The Story, Part 1
sections.text:
Several generations after Adam and Eve, the earth had filled with people — and with wickedness. The Bible says that God saw that the wickedness of man was great in the earth, and that every imagination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil continually. The world God had made very good had become full of violence. And it grieved God at His heart.

But in the middle of that darkness, there is one bright line. Genesis chapter six, verse eight says: “But Noah found grace in the eyes of the LORD.” Grace means favor that is given, not earned. The next verse tells us that Noah was a just man, and that Noah walked with God.

God told Noah that He would bring a flood of waters upon the earth. And He gave Noah very specific instructions: make an ark of gopher wood. Make rooms in it, and cover it inside and out with pitch. God gave its exact measurements — three hundred cubits long, fifty cubits wide, and thirty cubits high. That is roughly as long as one and a half football fields. Noah was to bring his family into the ark, along with animals of every kind, and food for them all.

Imagine being Noah. He had probably never seen anything like the flood God described. He was building an enormous boat on dry land, and the work would take many years. Surely people watched and wondered. But the Bible gives a simple, powerful summary of Noah's response, in Genesis chapter six, verse twenty-two: “Thus did Noah; according to all that God commanded him, so did he.”

sections.title: The Story, Part 2
sections.text:
When the ark was finished, God told Noah to go in. Noah, his wife, his three sons — Shem, Ham, and Japheth — and their three wives entered the ark. Eight people in all. The animals came too, just as God had said. And then the Bible includes a beautiful detail: “and the LORD shut him in.” God Himself closed the door.

Then the fountains of the great deep were broken up, and the windows of heaven were opened. Genesis chapter seven, verse twelve says: “And the rain was upon the earth forty days and forty nights.” The waters rose higher and higher until even the high mountains were covered. Every living thing on the dry land died. Only Noah, and those with him in the ark, remained alive.

The waters stayed on the earth for a long time. But God remembered Noah. He made a wind pass over the earth, and the waters began to go down. The ark came to rest on the mountains of Ararat. Noah waited. He sent out a raven, and then a dove. The first time, the dove found no place to rest and came back. Seven days later, Noah sent the dove out again, and that evening it returned with an olive leaf in its mouth. Now Noah knew the waters were going down. Seven days after that, he sent the dove out once more, and this time it did not return.

When the earth was dry, God told Noah to come out of the ark with his family and all the animals. And the very first thing Noah did was build an altar and worship the Lord.

Then God made a covenant — a solemn promise — with Noah and with every living creature. He promised that never again would a flood destroy all life on the earth. And He gave a sign. Genesis chapter nine, verse thirteen: “I do set my bow in the cloud, and it shall be for a token of a covenant between me and the earth.”

sections.title: The Lesson
sections.text:
What can we learn from Noah?

First, God takes sin seriously. The flood reminds us that evil is not a small thing to God. He is holy, and He is just.

Second, God provides a way of rescue. The same God who judged the world also gave instructions for an ark. Many Christians have seen the ark as a picture of Jesus. Just as everyone inside the ark was safe, everyone who trusts in Christ is safe in Him.

Third, faith shows itself in obedience. Noah didn't just believe God in his head; he picked up his tools and started building, and he kept building year after year. Faithfulness often looks ordinary: doing the next right thing that God has asked of you, even when no one else understands, and even when you can't yet see the result.

And fourth, God keeps His promises. Every time you see a rainbow, you can remember that God has never broken His word. Not once.

sections.title: Prayer and Reflection
sections.text:
Take a moment to think: is there something God has been asking you to do, but you've been waiting until it feels easier or until others approve? What would it look like to obey today, like Noah did?

Let's pray. Lord God, thank You for Your grace, which I could never earn. Thank You for providing a way of rescue through Jesus. Give me the courage to obey You even when it's hard and when others don't understand. And when I see a rainbow, remind me that You always keep Your promises. In Jesus' name, Amen.

Thank you for listening. Next time, we'll meet a man named Abraham, who left everything to follow God.
